title: 'Asr, the afternoon prayer
tomorrow: dinner at Jordan's grandma's starts right at sunset. what then?

cards: Saturday, three-forty. Lunch is long gone, dinner is hours off, and the afternoon has gone soft: one more store, one more episode, one more game. Nobody plans to lose the afternoon.
It just slides. The Qur'an names exactly one prayer to guard, and it isn't the dawn one. In Pickthall's words: "Be guardians of your prayers, and of the midmost prayer."
Which one is the midmost? The reports in Bukhari and Muslim answer: 'Asr, the afternoon prayer. The one that sits in the slide.

teach.b: The verse doesn't say 'Asr by name; it says al-wusta, the midmost. The hadith fill it in.

teach.h: KEPT FROM IT AT THE TRENCH.
teach.b: On the day of the Trench, with Medina under siege, the fighting kept the Prophet ﷺ from praying 'Asr until the sun had set, and he was deeply distressed. He called it the middle prayer, the 'Asr prayer.
So even he knew the afternoon could be taken from you, not by laziness, but by a full day.

In Sahih al-Bukhari he gives the stakes in a picture: whoever misses 'Asr is like someone who has lost his family and his property. A strong image for a quiet hour. What does a person do with that this week?
Three things the tradition hands over.
One: guard it means plan it. 'Asr is the prayer most likely to fall inside an outing, a practice, a shift, so it gets a spot before the afternoon starts. Two: the place is already there.
In another report in Bukhari, the Prophet says the earth has been made a place of prayer for him. A clean corner of a park, a quiet stairwell, a parked car's back seat when there's nothing else.
Three: when the day really does run over, as it did at the Trench, grief is the right response, not a shrug.

how: 'Asr is prayed in the afternoon, from mid-afternoon until shortly before sunset; Muslims who are out often pray it in a park, a quiet room or any clean place, and schools of law differ slightly on when its time begins.

o: the afternoon prayer, said as the light starts to lean
the evening prayer, said as the sun goes down
a short extra prayer said only on Saturdays

games.q: the afternoon prayer — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an names 'Asr in the verse about guarding the middle prayer
the verse says the midmost prayer; the hadith identify it as 'Asr.
the Prophet himself was once kept from 'Asr until after sunset
on the day of the Trench, and he was deeply distressed by it.

games.q: a friend's birthday at a trampoline park runs all afternoon, past sunset. 'Asr has come in. what does guarding it look like?
o: pray it later with Maghrib, once the party's over.
leave the party now and go pray it at home.
find a quiet clean spot, pray, then go back and jump.
games.why: guarding it doesn't mean leaving the party; the earth is a place of prayer. it means not letting the afternoon slide past it.

practice: Look at your own afternoon tomorrow, hour by hour, and find the one plan most likely to swallow it. Name a real spot nearby where a few quiet minutes would fit: a corner, a bench, a car.
Then sit, and see that spot as clearly as you can, the floor, the light, the sound around it.

wordCard.voice: 'Asr: the afternoon prayer, prayed while the light starts to lean. In the hadith, the midmost prayer the Qur'an says to guard.

orig.note: Arabic: afternoon, the part of the day when the light begins to decline.

carryVoice: Tuck this in for the afternoon: guard the middle prayer, the one that sits in the slide. See you after sunset.
